# ETL Load Order

Load order in a [[star-schema]] is not a style choice. Declared foreign keys make it a hard
dependency graph: every dimension a fact references must be populated before the fact is inserted, or
the insert fails. The interesting part is what you populate the *dimension* from.

## The dependency chain, as built

In [[data-warehousing-and-business-intelligence]], the retail load runs in six stages:

1. `DIM_TIME` — from the source order-header table
2. `DIM_CUSTOMER` — a `LEFT JOIN` chain plus an `OUTER APPLY` for the primary address
3. `DIM_PRODUCT` — independent of 2
4. `DIM_SALESPERSON` — independent of 2 and 3
5. `FACT_SALES` — joins the source header to its detail rows
6. **verification** — a `UNION ALL` row-count roll-call across all five tables, then two anti-join
   referential-integrity checks

Stages 2–4 are mutually independent and could run in any order or in parallel; only the
dimension→fact edge is real. Stage 6 is the subject of [[verify-the-load-dont-declare-it]].

## The counter-case that makes the rule concrete

The obvious way to build a calendar dimension is to select the distinct dates *out of the fact table*
— it is the smaller, more relevant set. The source comment writes out why that deadlocks: the
dimension would be built from an empty fact, the fact load would then find no matching parent rows
for its foreign keys, and the warehouse "would build cleanly and contain nothing". Building
`DIM_TIME` from the **source** header instead — a `UNION` of order dates and ship dates, because
[[star-schema|the calendar is role-played twice]] — breaks the cycle.

This is the transferable form of the rule: **a dimension must be sourced from upstream of the fact,
never from the fact it serves.** A build that succeeds and produces nothing is the failure mode to
design against, because it does not raise an error.

## Truncate-and-rebuild, not incremental

Every load here is full rebuild — the DDL opens with `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS`. There is no
change-data-capture, no watermark column, no merge, and no slowly-changing-dimension handling
anywhere in the repository. That simplifies ordering enormously: with no history to preserve, the
only constraint is the FK graph. It also makes [[surrogate-vs-natural-keys|natural keys]] sufficient.

## Staging as a separate stage

The price mart adds a landing step first: [[ssis]] moves a flat file into a `staging.quotes` table
that carries `CHECK` constraints at the door (high ≥ low with open and close bounded by both;
non-negative volume), so malformed rows are rejected before any modelling happens. Then the star
loads, then a separate script backfills the derived indicator — see [[window-function-frames]].
Rejecting bad input at the boundary rather than downstream is the same discipline as
[[separating-computation-from-io]].
